name: Lonicera

project_scope.selection_mode: approved source-pool all three staged for canonical install
project_scope.learner_vs_range_note: L. japonica is a non-native encounter/comparison taxon; approved source-pool admission does not imply native range PASS. Other taxa also retain separate county-range determinations.
project_scope.note: Do not confuse species cards in canonical learner with BONAP target-native PASS. albiflora and sempervirens unresolved; japonica introduced comparison.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: At a node, confirm opposite simple leaves. Trace an intact flower from corolla tube to its INFERIOR ovary. Then ask whether the flowers come in axillary pairs (Japanese honeysuckle) or condensed TERMINAL whorls. On terminal flowering shoots, measure the corolla and photograph the fused bracts: both L. albiflora and L. sempervirens can have a fused perfoliate pair, so that character alone does NOT separate them.
shared_traits: Woody shrubs, scrambling shrubs or vines with opposite simple leaves, typically with entire margins and without stipules.
Sympetalous flowers with a tubular base, five corolla lobes (often appearing two-lipped), five stamens and an inferior ovary.
Fleshy berries with small seeds; ripe fruit color is especially helpful for routing L. japonica versus the two red-fruited species.
shared_genus_recognition.false_friend: Fused terminal bracts are not exclusive to coral honeysuckle. Texas honeysuckle L. albiflora also has connate-perfoliate inflorescence bracts and sometimes perfoliate sucker leaves.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: flowering shoot: insertion points of inflorescences
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Flowers in small opposite axillary PAIRS at successive nodes, rather than terminal condensed whorls -> L. japonica candidate.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: terminal flowering cluster, floral corolla length and lobing
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Terminal whorls with short (~17–20 mm) clearly two-lipped cream flowers -> L. albiflora; terminal whorls with long (~38–48 mm) mostly tubular flowers and relatively short lobes -> L. sempervirens.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: ripe berry associated with the identified flowering shoot
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Blackish fruit supports L. japonica; red-orange to scarlet fruit can occur in BOTH L. albiflora and L. sempervirens and cannot split them.

look_here_first_sequence.inspect: vegetative-only vine or unusual flowering shoot
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Retain Lonicera sp. when no terminal/axillary structure or flower dissection is available; leaf fusion by itself is insufficient.

species_comparison_matrix.Lonicera albiflora: Often a several-stemmed arching shrub to ~1.4 m with some twining branches.
species_comparison_matrix.Lonicera japonica: Evergreen or semi-evergreen scandent/sprawling vine, often with pubescent young shoots.

species_comparison_matrix.character: leaf attachment and upper shoot bracts
species_comparison_matrix.Lonicera albiflora: Usually separate short-petiolate ordinary leaves (petiole often ≤3 mm), BUT inflorescence bracts strongly fused/perfoliate; vigorous shoots can have fused leaves.
species_comparison_matrix.Lonicera japonica: Ordinary opposite leaves distinct with petioles typically ~5–15 mm, not a large complete fused disk immediately subtending terminal whorls.
species_comparison_matrix.Lonicera sempervirens: Ordinary opposite leaves separate, petiole often ≤7 mm; one or two uppermost terminal pairs/bracts strongly connate into a cup or disk.
species_comparison_matrix.weight: critical structural caution: leaf fusion cannot separate albiflora from sempervirens

species_comparison_matrix.Lonicera albiflora: Condensed terminal cymes, often in whorls, to ~13 flowers.
species_comparison_matrix.Lonicera japonica: Paired axillary 2-flowered cymes along leafy shoot nodes.
species_comparison_matrix.Lonicera sempervirens: Terminal condensed whorls / interrupted spike-like cluster, sometimes many flowers.

species_comparison_matrix.Lonicera albiflora: Cream to white, two-lipped, ~17–19.5 mm; tube/throat ~9 mm, lobes conspicuously expanded.
species_comparison_matrix.Lonicera japonica: Long ~45–57 mm, strongly two-lipped, long tube ~24–27 mm with long projecting lobes, white aging yellow.
species_comparison_matrix.Lonicera sempervirens: Elongate ~38–48 mm narrow trumpet; lobes relatively short and nearly regular compared with the tube; red/orange outside often yellow inside.
species_comparison_matrix.weight: PRIMARY: architecture + length; not color alone

species_comparison_matrix.Lonicera albiflora: Typically glabrous, sometimes glaucous stems and leaves.
species_comparison_matrix.Lonicera japonica: Young shoots and petioles short-hairy; stalked glandular hairs can be visible with magnification.
species_comparison_matrix.Lonicera sempervirens: Young shoots relatively smooth; leaf underside may be glaucous and minutely hairy.

species_comparison_matrix.Lonicera albiflora: Red-orange to scarlet berry, ~6.5–10 mm diameter.
species_comparison_matrix.Lonicera japonica: Blackish berry, usually ~6–8 mm, up to ~12 seeds in UT account.
species_comparison_matrix.weight: PRIMARY for japonica vs others, NOT albiflora vs sempervirens

scientific_cautions: Never teach perfoliate leaves as unique to L. sempervirens: A. C. Gibson describes connate terminal bracts and occasional fused sucker leaves in L. albiflora.
Ripe red berries do not split L. albiflora from L. sempervirens. Floral architecture and corolla measurements are the reliable training pair.
L. japonica is a non-native introduced comparison in the source pool; avoid labeling it as a native Hays County plant.
Winter leaf persistence varies by weather and microclimate; evergreen/deciduous is supporting only.
Flowers of L. japonica age from white toward yellow; flower color alone is not species proof.
A connected low leaf ledge is not the same as the wide fused perfoliate disk below terminal flowers. Show exact node and contiguous blade tissue.
Photos with no attached inflorescence origin or no ruler may be useful as provisional portraits, not a completed diagnostic pair.
No species files, range statuses, or native-only counts were changed by this genus lesson.

local_lookalike_routing.test: Opposite simple leaves and berries may look similar; compare much shorter, smaller bell-shaped flowers and fruit arrangement with Lonicera's extended tubular corolla and head/axillary flower layout.

Opposite foliage and inferior ovary are shared Dipsacales traits; Viburnum commonly has broad many-flowered clusters of small relatively regular flowers and drupes rather than Lonicera tubular flowers and berries.
Long orange-red tubes can resemble coral honeysuckle, but Campsis leaves are oppositely PINNATELY COMPOUND and climber uses aerial rootlets; Lonicera leaves are simple.
Potential planting/trade look-alikes to L. sempervirens; document provenance and compare accepted hybrid identity rather than certifying a garden plant as straight-species native.

diagnostic_photo_requirements.role: uppermost fused leaf pair and flower stalk

diagnostic_photo_requirements.role: japonica leaf-node and young-stem gland hair macro
diagnostic_photo_requirements.show: separate petioles and axillary inflorescence; hairs and stalked glands with mm ruler
